clue.text: Original man? That's me!

definitions.meaning: the first human being created, Adam in the Genesis story
the grammatical person used for a speaker referring to themself, I or me

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being the original model of manhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam was literally the earliest human, and grammar names the speaking 'I' with the same phrase, so both senses share one expression.

clue.text: Invigorates one fellow in his prime

indicators.note: in places the short pieces for one and fellow within the phrase for his prime

parts.note: a man's forties are often called his prime of life
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man at the peak of life is full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I (one) and F (fellow) inside FORTIES, a man's prime years.
explanation.definitionFit: To fortify is to strengthen, giving fresh energy and vigour.

clue.text: Somehow I reused what was left

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of the following words are arranged in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: Someone muses on having reused whatever was left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges the letters of I REUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder, the material left behind afterwards.

clue.text: Chemical indicator one has to examine daily

parts.note: to examine is to test
a daily is a newspaper published every day, a paper

explanation.surface: A lab worker must check a chemical indicator every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like an adverb but is a noun here: a daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper is a strip used in chemistry to show acidity, an example of an indicator strip.

clue.text: In the meantime a sedative gave relief

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Meanwhile a sedative brought comfort to the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' says the answer sits inside 'meantime a sedative', across the end of meantime, all of a and the start of sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain is to lessen it, bringing comfort.

clue.text: Trip's cancellation brings unexpected benefit

parts.note: a spin is a short trip or drive, as in going for a spin
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: Calling off a journey turns out to have an unforeseen upside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' reads as a journey being cancelled, but here it is just a short drive; the possessive is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-off is a by-product, an incidental advantage arising from something else.

clue.text: Anything but an Anglican at present

parts.note: the prefix non means not, anything but
CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Someone at the moment is anything other than a member of the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the idiom 'for the nonce', meaning for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: The nonce is the current occasion, so the idiom 'for the nonce' means for now, for the time being.

clue.text: Fun and games for early risers

definitions.meaning: people who get up at dawn are called ..., after the bird that sings at daybreak

explanation.surface: Merriment is laid on for those who get up at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both playful mischief and the songbird whose dawn song names morning people.

clue.text: The humanities require abundant skills

parts.note: liberal can mean generous or plentiful
arts are skills or crafts

explanation.surface: Studying the humanities calls for a wealth of talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature, history and philosophy form the traditional academic subjects grouped under this name.

clue.text: A lesson is revised termly

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A school lesson gets updated every term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is revised' rearranges the letters of A LESSON IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held each term or session of a school or court year occurs termly.

clue.text: Went bananas after having mislaid the paper

definitions.meaning: to go bananas is to fly into a rage
read literally: a person who lost their newspaper, rag being slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone flew into a fury once their newspaper went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag is slang for a cheap newspaper, so the idiom for losing your temper is read literally as misplacing the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing your temper is the idiom, while a literal reading has a person misplacing a tabloid.

clue.text: Erect skyscrapers to gain promotion

definitions.meaning: to construct tall buildings is to build upwards
publicity that hypes something in advance

explanation.surface: Putting up tall towers is a way for a developer to win advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: Building upwards describes constructing towers, and a media campaign creating hype is also known by the same phrase.

clue.text: Many tramps become herdsmen

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
rovers are wanderers or vagrants

explanation.surface: A crowd of vagrants find work tending livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' is a crossword convention for a big Roman numeral, here D for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Drovers drive cattle or sheep to market, so they are herders of livestock.

clue.text: I entered wreck from rear

indicators.note: entered means went into, so the letter I goes inside the word for wreck

parts.note: rase is a variant spelling of raze, to demolish

explanation.surface: Someone came into a crashed vehicle from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' looks like the back of the wreck, but it is the verb: to bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children or animals is to bring them up, nurture them.

clue.text: Left a page in folder

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a folio is a single leaf or page of a book

explanation.surface: A sheet has been left behind inside a file.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat case for carrying loose papers or artwork.

clue.text: Naked courage needed to take undiluted liquor

parts.note: raw can mean bare or exposed
spirit is mettle or bravery

explanation.surface: Sheer nerve is required to drink strong alcohol neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmixed alcohol straight from distillation is called by this name, strong and uncut.

clue.text: Surprisingly, I rout able party aficionado

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker is amazed to have defeated a capable opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges the letters of I ROUT ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of Britain's Labour Party is an enthusiast for that political party.

clue.text: One blow too many for former foreign secretary

parts.note: last can mean previous, as in last year
Jack Straw was the British Foreign Secretary from 2001 to 2006

explanation.surface: A past holder of a high government post is named.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the final setback that breaks the camel's back, from the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial final addition that causes a collapse; one more burden than can be borne.

clue.text: Drag one's feet before card game starts

definitions.meaning: to walk without lifting the feet properly
mixing the pack is what players do before dealing

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles before a game of cards begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambling along is one sense; mixing the deck before a hand is the other.

clue.text: Saunter whilst doc's in the drink

indicators.note: in means the doctor's letters go inside the word for the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A stroll while the doctor is in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' suggests the sea, but here it is beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll at a leisurely pace is to walk slowly and casually.

clue.text: Shorten a spanner

parts.note: a bridge spans a river or gap

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut down a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' looks like the tool but is anything that spans.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down, making it shorter.

clue.text: Solitary man about to compile clues

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: compile means put together, so the letters of clues are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: A loner sets about writing crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compile' looks like the setter's job of writing clues, but it is the signal to rearrange that word's letters; 'about' is the short preposition used in memos.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives withdrawn from society, a hermit.

clue.text: Footwear made from many pieces of wood

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
logs are chunks of timber

explanation.surface: Shoes made of lots of wooden parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Clogs are heavy shoes with wooden soles.

clue.text: Black oriental of emaciated frame

parts.note: E stands for east, the orient
a thin, skeletal body is bony

explanation.surface: A thin person from the East with dark colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is the very dark wood, used for the colour deep black.

clue.text: Chief steward accommodated society hunter

indicators.note: accommodated means took in, so the letter for society goes inside

parts.note: a purser is the officer in charge of a ship's stewards and accounts
U means upper class, polite society

explanation.surface: A ship's officer took in a socialite who hunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief' is not a first-letter signal here: a chief steward on a ship is the purser. U for upper class comes from the British 'U and non-U' distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chases or follows is a chaser, a hunter after its quarry.

clue.text: Betray and quell unionised workers

parts.note: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them
to floor is to overwhelm or defeat

explanation.surface: Someone betrays and suppresses the union members.
explanation.definitionFit: The production staff in a factory, as opposed to management, are typically trade union members.

clue.text: Discharging duties may exhaust German leader

parts.note: to do in is slang for wearing out completely

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Carrying out his duties may wear out the head of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German leader' suggests a chancellor, but it just means the first letter of German.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing a task is carrying it out, the activity of getting things done.

clue.text: What empathetic ophthalmologists should do?

parts.note: eye doctors who understand one another would agree, and their work literally involves looking into people's eyes

explanation.surface: A question about how understanding eye doctors ought to behave.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to agree completely, while eye specialists also literally examine one eye against another.
